headline: Bruins cruise to shutout win while Sox look for answers
morning_brew: It was a tale of two nights in the Hub, starting with a dominant show at the Garden. Our Bruins looked like they hadn't missed a beat from training camp, shutting out the Rangers to kick off the regular season. Fraser Minten played like a man possessed, breaking the tie late before JJ Peterka and Mark Kastelic piled on to seal it. Jeremy Swayman was an absolute wall in the crease, turning away every single shot that came his way. It was the kind of composed, start-to-finish effort that makes you feel like maybe, just maybe, this winter won't be a complete frozen nightmare.

Then you look at what happened in the Bronx, and man, I need a nap to recover from that one. The Red Sox got completely outclassed in the playoff opener, and watching the Yankees put up runs in bunches while our bats stayed frozen was a special kind of misery. We never got anything going, and the bullpen implosion in the late innings turned a tough night into a total disaster. I don't care who we're playing; you can't show up to the postseason and expect to survive with three hits. It felt like watching Uncle Carmine try to assemble IKEA furniture with no instructions — painful and doomed from the start.

We have to turn the page and get our heads right for the next one in the series tonight. It's a quick turnaround at Yankee Stadium, and the pressure is ratcheted up about as high as it can go this early in the bracket. My neighbor Rick has been pacing his porch since the final out yesterday, muttering about lineup adjustments and situational hitting, and for once I am not gonna argue with him. We need a clean, focused effort to even things up before this thing gets out of hand, because the Bronx isn't exactly a place where you want to dig yourself a hole.

news_digest.headline: Fraser Minten shines as late surge lifts the Bruins past the Rangers 3-0
news_digest.dans_take: A perfect start to the year, and I'm already clearing space on the shelf for the trophy.

news_digest.headline: Schlittler and Rice torment hometown team as Yankees beat rival Red Sox 9-0 in playoff opener
news_digest.dans_take: Absolutely brutal night for our guys, and frankly, we have to show up with a pulse tonight.
